mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 5.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.5% over 3 months signals labor market tightening that increases consumer spending and corporate profit expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in residential housing starts (HOUST > 1300) and consumer spending (RSAFS > 380000) indicate robust housing and consumption cycles that elevate corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST exceeds 1300 and RSAFS exceeds 380000.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 110.0 indicates manufacturing expansion that increases corporate output and profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above 11500 billion dollars (GDPC1) indicates sustained economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through extended profit momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 exceeds 11500.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 207.5) triggers monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate market repricing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 207.5.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent unemployment decline (UNRATE < 4.8%) and payroll growth (PAYEMS > 138000) signal labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.8 and PAYEMS exceeds 138000.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline below 110.0 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through earnings downgrade pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 110.0.
